correctness.rationale: For every finite connected cactus, the cycle rank of each induced subgraph equals the number of fully retained original cycle blocks; Euler’s identity gives \(\mu_G(p)=np-ep^2+\sum_jp^{\ell_j}\). Direct Bernoulli score differentiation gives \(\operatorname{Cov}(N_p,C_p)=p(1-p)\mu_G'(p)\). The derivative polynomial is convex and has one positive-to-negative interior zero except for K2 and C3. A block decomposition and exact sign inequalities at the algebraic four-cycle root and 3/4 establish the sharp extremal interval; the P3 path and bouquets of C4 attain/approach endpoints. An exact-identity checker ran on 746 small cactus graphs with 1550 checks. Finite experiments are not used as proof of the infinite result.

value.rationale: Natural finite-network fragmentation objective: expected count of surviving connected clusters. The result identifies exactly when increasing retention switches from creating to consolidating components, uniformly over all cactus topologies; all optimizer locations lie in a sharp algebraic interval, with a uniquely extremizing three-site path at the upper end and a counterintuitive four-cycle bouquet infimum. The explicit cycle-length statistic is needed for precise planning of density levels, and \(K_4\) witnesses an essential boundary beyond cactus graphs. The theorem is not presented as an infinite-cluster critical point.
